introduction: On this fourth Sunday of Advent, Isaiah gives King Ahaz a sign: the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and name him Emmanuel. In the Gospel, Joseph, a righteous man, learns in a dream that Mary's child is from the Holy Spirit, and he takes her into his home. Paul speaks of the Gospel of God's Son, descended from David. Christmas is very near. Let us welcome Emmanuel, God with us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God is with us in Jesus Christ. Let us bring our prayers to the Father as Christmas draws near.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim to all the world that God is with us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For fathers, and for all who protect and care for families: that they may be faithful like Saint Joseph. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those facing difficult decisions: that they may listen to God's word and trust him as Joseph did. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who will spend Christmas alone, in sorrow or in fear: that they may know that God is with them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make room in our hearts and homes for Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you sent your Son to be Emmanuel, God with us. Give us the faith of Joseph and Mary, so that we may welcome him with joy at Christmas. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: God with us
reflection.body:
King Ahaz faces a threat from enemy armies and does not want to trust God. When Isaiah invites him to ask for a sign, he refuses with false piety. God gives a sign anyway: "Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The name means God with us.

Matthew tells us how this sign was fulfilled, and he tells it from Joseph's side. Mary is engaged to Joseph, and before they live together, "she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit." Joseph does not yet know about the Holy Spirit. He only knows that the child is not his. Matthew tells us he was "a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example," so he decides to end the engagement quietly. His goodness combines respect for the law with mercy.

Then God speaks to him in a dream: "Joseph, son of David, don't be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit." The angel tells him to name the child Jesus, "for it is he who shall save his people from their sins." And Matthew sees in this the fulfillment of Isaiah's words: "They shall call his name Immanuel," which is, being interpreted, "God with us."

Joseph wakes and does exactly what the angel told him. He never speaks in the Gospels, but his obedience makes room for Jesus to be born into the house of David.

Paul tells us that this Son, "born of the offspring of David according to the flesh," is "declared to be the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead."

In these last days before Christmas, imitate Joseph: listen for what God is asking, and do it without delay. Make room for Emmanuel in your heart and home.
